search.name: Broken citations
search.see: A link that loads but does not say what the answer says. Some links never existed.
search.why: Links are attached after the text is written, from a pool of snippets and copies. Nothing checks that the page holds the sentence.
search.numl: of 1,600 citation tests named the wrong article, publisher or URL
search.fix: A separate checker ties each claim to a quoted sentence on a page it opened. Claims it cannot tie are dropped or marked.
search.you: Ask for a verbatim quote next to each key claim, then open two links yourself.

search.name: Silent failure
search.see: A finished, confident report when the search found nothing or the tool broke.
search.why: Guessing scores better than saying "I don't know", and tool errors often come back looking like success.
search.numl: of answers that used planted content gave no warning
search.fix: Show every failed search, blocked page and spent budget above the answer. Never deliver a report with zero opened sources.
search.you: End research prompts with: list the searches you ran, the pages you opened, and anything that failed.

search.name: Stops too early
search.see: Few sources, generic queries, and the key page never found.
search.why: Agents stop when they feel confident, not when each part of the question has evidence.
search.numl: of errors on same-day news came from retrieval, not reasoning
search.fix: Split the question into sub-questions and stop only when each has evidence or a clear "not found".
search.you: Use deep research mode for multi-part questions and ask for the plan first.

search.name: Planted sources win
search.see: SEO lists, vendor pages, one forum comment or a scam phone number presented as fact.
search.why: Ranking rewards relevance, not reliability. Many copies of one planted page look like agreement.
search.numl: AI search platforms cited a made-up concept within 7 days
search.fix: Label every source by publisher, date and type, and count copies as one source. Use allow and block lists for high-stakes work.
search.you: Ask for primary sources and who published each one.

search.name: Stale facts
search.see: Last year's figure, a former office holder, old install steps.
search.why: Snippets and caches lag the live page, and the model's sense of today drifts toward its training date.
search.numl: more outdated answers when built from snippets than from opened pages
search.fix: Give the model today's date and open the page for any fact that changes. Show the page date next to each figure.
search.you: Start with "As of today" and ask for the date next to every number.

search.name: Snippets, not pages
search.see: An answer built from a search snippet or a cut-down summary of the page.
search.why: Opening pages costs time and tokens. Some tools pass the page through a smaller model first.
search.numl: of search episodes where one leading model opened no page at all
search.fix: Read before cite: only cite pages that were opened, and report any page that was cut.
search.you: Ask it to open every source it cites and quote the exact sentence it used from each page.

search.name: Blocked pages
search.see: The best source is paywalled, bot-blocked or built in JavaScript, so the answer leans on copies.
search.why: Sites are closing the door to AI bots, and many AI fetchers do not run JavaScript.
search.numl: AI-bot blocking now covers ad pages on existing free sites on a major network
search.fix: Label each blocked fetch, then route to a browser, a document parser or a licensed source. Never evade blocks.
search.you: Paste or upload the source yourself when it matters.

search.name: False premise
search.see: The wrong fact in your question is accepted and "confirmed" with sources.
search.why: Models are tuned to agree, and the premise gets written into the search query.
search.numl: of fabricated facts accepted by one leading model
search.fix: Check the question's assumptions before searching, and flag any that fail.
search.you: Ask neutral questions first, then ask for the best evidence against your view.

search.name: Memory beats search
search.see: An answer from training data when search was on, or a correct memory overwritten by a bad page.
search.why: The model's own confidence decides what to trust, and that confidence is poorly calibrated.
search.numl: of cases where models took wrong retrieved text over correct memory
search.fix: Show disagreements between memory and evidence, and prefer dated primary pages for facts that change.
search.you: Require a dated primary source for prices, rules and people in roles.

search.name: Planted instructions
search.see: Usually nothing. Hidden text on a page steers the answer or tells an agent to act.
search.why: One model reads data and instructions together and cannot reliably tell them apart.
search.numl: of injected attacks on real pages got past a standard browsing planner
search.fix: Partly fixed at the top: leading products now ship injection filters. For any agent that can act, read pages in a separate model with no tools. Read-only research can use injection filters.
search.you: Never give a browsing agent your email, payments or private files.

frontier.name: Confident wrong answers in high-stakes work
frontier.see: A fluent answer with invented case law, a wrong figure or an unneeded medical test, and the error only shows up later in court or with a client.
frontier.why: The model sounds just as sure when it is wrong, and people often use the output without checking.
frontier.numl: court cases now listed with AI-invented content
frontier.fix: A named person checks every citation and figure before anything is filed or sent. Record which model produced which output.

frontier.name: Agents act or report wrongly
frontier.see: An agent deletes files, touches production, uses saved passwords, or says tests pass when the last run came before its own edits.
frontier.why: Agents get broad permissions by default, and few teams can trace what an agent actually did.
frontier.numl: "tests pass" claims in one team's audit had no up-to-date test run behind them
frontier.fix: Give agents the least access they need and an approval step before delete or deploy. Accept a pass only with a captured test log.

frontier.name: Data leaks out
frontier.see: Staff paste company data into personal AI accounts. Consumers learn from lawsuits that allege their chats were used without valid consent.
frontier.why: Policies alone do not stop it, and uploads were highest where AI was banned.
frontier.numl: of employees who use AI uploaded company information to public AI tools
frontier.fix: Give staff an approved tool with controls that stop company data leaving, and check what each vendor may do with your chats.

frontier.name: Agent tools as an attack path
frontier.see: A hidden instruction in a repo, web page or plug-in makes a coding tool leak secrets or run code on a developer's machine.
frontier.why: Agent tools treat text they read as instructions, and some vendors decline to treat these chains as flaws.
frontier.numl: severity out of 10 for a Copilot flaw in Visual Studio triggered by a hidden instruction
frontier.fix: Treat repos, plug-ins and tool settings as untrusted, keep agents off the open internet by default, and patch agent tools quickly.

frontier.name: Spend without proven return
frontier.see: AI budgets keep rising while finance teams still cannot see which uses pay back.
frontier.why: Few firms compare value with cost, and few set rules for stopping a pilot.
frontier.numl: of CIOs report significant or transformational value from AI, in a survey of 2,002 tech leaders
frontier.fix: Track value against cost for each use case, and write the stop rule before each pilot starts.

frontier.name: Models change under you
frontier.see: The model behaves differently after an update, an old model disappears, or an API model is retired and calls start failing.
frontier.why: Vendors replace models to free capacity, and default settings change too.
frontier.numl: OpenAI model IDs shut down in one day
frontier.fix: Pin model versions, keep a register of retirement dates and rerun your own tests before accepting any change.

frontier.name: Usage caps nobody can predict
frontier.see: A paid allowance runs out far faster than expected, and there is no way to tell in advance what a task will cost.
frontier.why: Vendors reprice and cut allowances often, compute is scarce, and meters are not documented.
frontier.numl: pricing and limit changes across AI tools in one quarter
frontier.fix: Write notice periods for limit changes into contracts, track usage per task and ask vendors for a cost preview.

frontier.name: Tells people what they want to hear
frontier.see: The assistant agrees, praises and goes along. Most people do not notice. Vulnerable users can be pulled deeper into harmful beliefs.
frontier.why: Models tend to go along with the person in front of them. Eight US states now allege the design itself is too agreeable.
frontier.numl: US states sued OpenAI on the same day over ChatGPT safety
frontier.fix: If you run a consumer chat product, add crisis routing, age checks and instructions against blind agreement. Test them on your own chats.

frontier.name: Controls lag behind rollout
frontier.see: Agents go live faster than anyone can list, trace or switch them off. Regulators have started asking vendors questions.
frontier.why: Rollout plans run ahead of governance. This month the EU AI Office sent its first information requests and the FTC sent subpoenas.
frontier.numl: of organisations plan AI agents within a year, against those with governance for them
frontier.tag: Analyst survey of 2,000+ tech leaders, Q2 2026
frontier.fix: Keep a list of every agent, with full traces and a kill switch you have tested.

frontier.name: Review overload and workforce strain
frontier.see: People spend more time checking AI output, maintainers face a flood of low-quality AI submissions, and some roles are being cut.
frontier.why: Output grows faster than review capacity, and rework eats the time AI saved.
frontier.numl: of incoming code changes are low-quality AI work, say open-source maintainers
frontier.fix: Plan roles and review capacity around the volume AI produces, not the old workload.

frontier.name: Loses context and instructions
frontier.see: The assistant forgets earlier decisions, ignores house rules or invents context it never had.
frontier.why: Long chats get compressed, sometimes to save cost when space remains, and rules in a prompt are advice the model can drop.
frontier.numl: coding sessions lost working context overnight in one user's log
frontier.fix: Keep key rules and decisions in files the tool reloads, and enforce house rules outside the model.

frontier.name: Outages and capacity shortfalls
frontier.see: Errors and slowdowns in the middle of a task, sometimes while the status page says all is well.
frontier.why: Compute is tight, and a single fault can block every product a vendor runs at once.
frontier.numl: outage reports for one Gemini outage while its status page showed no issue
frontier.fix: Fail over across providers, and alert on spend-limit and capacity errors.

frontier.name: Safety filters block the wrong things
frontier.see: Normal work is refused or flagged, while some harmful requests still get through.
frontier.why: Filters trade false alarms against misses, so normal work gets caught along with real risks.
frontier.numl: of reasonable safety research tasks refused by three Anthropic models in a UK government test
frontier.tag: UK government test from last winter, reported Oct 2026
frontier.fix: Ask vendors for an appeal or allowlist path and their false-alarm rates.

frontier.name: Vendor lock-in
frontier.see: Moving a working AI tool to another provider takes far longer than planned, and price rises arrive that you cannot avoid.
frontier.why: Model names are hard-coded, prompts are tuned to one model, and business plans limit what you can export.
frontier.numl: of 520 tech leaders say switching costs made them delay, scale back or rework a move
frontier.fix: Keep model names in settings behind a gateway, own your tests and prompts, and write exit terms into contracts.
